judgment.explanation: The mention 此子 refers to 王長史 (Wang Huzhi / 王胡之), as confirmed by the Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-054-liu-annotation-003) which mentions '裒長史王胡之'. The supplied candidates are 王濛 (c0) and 王恭 (c1), neither of whom is 王胡之. The correct referent 王胡之 is missing from the candidate set.

何驃騎 refers to 何充 by his office title 驃騎. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-054-liu-annotation-001) explicitly identifies this as 何充, and annotation-002 uses 充 as the personal name. Candidate c0 (何充) is the correct referent. Candidate c1 (沈充) is a different person.
劉尹 refers to 劉遐, who held the office of 吏部尚書 (尹). The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-054-liu-annotation-003) explicitly mentions '吏部尚書劉遐'. Candidate c0 (劉遐) is the correct referent.

judgment.explanation: 真長 is the courtesy name of 劉惔 (Liu Tan). However, in this story, 真長 is used as the courtesy name for 劉尹/劉遐 (the 吏部尚書). The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-054-liu-annotation-003) identifies 吏部尚書劉遐 as the person being addressed. Candidate c0 (劉惔) matches the courtesy name 真長, and the annotation confirms this person is 劉遐. Candidate c1 (劉遐) is the same person but the courtesy name 真長 belongs to 劉惔. Given the annotation identifies 吏部尚書劉遐 as the referent, and 真長 is 劉惔's courtesy name, the identification of 真長 with 劉遐 (via 劉惔) is supported. Candidate c0 (劉惔) is the correct referent.
The annotation mentions 吏部尚書劉遐 who urged 裒, matching the candidate 劉遐. The surface 劉遐 is the full name of this person.

The annotation explicitly states 裒長史王胡之, indicating that 王長史 refers to 王胡之 (Wang Huzhi), not 王濛 (Wang Meng). The supplied candidate c0 is 王濛, which contradicts the evidence. The correct referent 王胡之 is not among the supplied candidates.

The 王 in the main text refers to 王長史, who is identified in the annotation as 王胡之 (裒長史王胡之). Neither candidate c0 (王恭) nor c1 (王濛) matches 王胡之. The correct referent is missing from the supplied candidates.

The annotation (别見/何充) cross-references 何充, and the surface 何充 is the full name of He Chong. Candidate c0 (何充) is the correct referent. Candidate c1 (沈充) is a different person with the same character 充 in the name.

The mention 充 refers to He Chong (何充). The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-054-liu-annotation-001) explicitly glosses the context with 何充, and annotation-002 mentions '充之卒' (Chong's death), confirming the single-character 充 refers to 何充. Candidate c1 (何充) is supported. Candidate c0 (沈充) is contradicted because the annotation context clearly identifies the referent as 何充, not 沈充.

review.explanation: The surface 何驃騎 is an office-title reference. The Liu annotation sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-054-liu-annotation-001 explicitly identifies the referent as 何充, and annotation-002 continues discussing 充's death (充之卒), matching the main text's 何驃騎亡後. The annotation evidence directly supports the identity resolution to 何充. No contradicting evidence exists.

The surface 劉尹 is an office-title reference. The Liu annotation sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-054-liu-annotation-003 explicitly mentions 吏部尚書劉遐, identifying the office-holder as 劉遐. The main text places 劉尹 as one of the two visitors alongside 王長史, and the annotation context (吏部尚書劉遐勸裒) matches this narrative. The annotation directly supports the identity resolution.

真長 is the courtesy name of 劉惔 (劉真長). However, the proposal resolves this mention to 劉遐 (candidate c0). The main text shows 禇 addressing 真長, and 真長 then responding. The Liu annotation sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-054-liu-annotation-003 identifies 吏部尚書劉遐 in this narrative context. The coreference chain links this mention to sfh1-mention-490780f4feba8e174d40cc0b (劉尹 = 劉遐). While 真長 is conventionally the courtesy name of 劉惔, the annotation evidence here identifies the person in this story as 劉遐, and the coreference structure within the text supports this. The annotation evidence specifically supports the identity as presented.

The surface 劉遐 directly matches the canonical name. The Liu annotation sfh1-ev-02-yanyu-054-liu-annotation-003 explicitly names 吏部尚書劉遐 in the context of this story, providing direct evidence that the person referenced is indeed 劉遐. The name match plus annotation identification supports the resolution.

The mention surface is 何充, the full name of He Chong. The Liu annotation (别見/何充) explicitly cross-references this person as 何充. The main text refers to 何驃騎 (He, the Cavalry General), and the annotation identifies this as 何充. The full name match plus the explicit annotation cross-reference provides specific evidence supporting identity with He Chong. No contradicting evidence is present.

The annotation evidence specifically supports the identity resolution of the abbreviated form 充 to He Chong. No contradicting evidence is present.

records.referent_role: the discussants/those who deliberated (about governance after He Chong's death)

周公 (Duke of Zhou) is a historical ruler/minister figure referenced by 王 (Wang) in the main text. Wang says '國自有周公' (the state naturally has its own Duke of Zhou), using the Duke of Zhou as a comparison for someone in the court. The mention is a ruler_title reference to the historical Duke of Zhou, not to any person present in the scene. It is distinct from all the other persons mentioned in the text. The comparison relation is between 王 (the speaker, sfh1-mention-ed62f5e748f376201352e71b) and 周公, where Wang asserts the state has its own Duke of Zhou figure.
records.referent_role: historical figure referenced as exemplary ruler/minister (Duke of Zhou)
